title: LinkedIn: Lessons from the Water Utility Ransomware Incident
body:
A regional water utility was hit by ransomware last month. Eleven servers encrypted, billing down for four days, historian data down for nine.

Here is the part that matters: the water kept flowing.

The treatment and distribution systems were segmented from the corporate network, so the malware never reached them. The intrusion started with a maintenance contractor's password that had not been changed in over a year and had no multi-factor authentication.

Three things every operator can do this week:
1. Rotate every third-party credential and turn on MFA for remote access.
2. Put your backups somewhere your domain admins cannot reach.
3. Practice the scenario where you have to cut the corporate and operational networks apart in a hurry.

Segmentation is not glamorous work. It is the reason this was a bad week instead of a public health emergency.
